name: Connector

claims.claim_text: The S-100 bus took its name from the 100-pin connector used in the MITS Altair; because the machine was an open design, other manufacturers standardised on that same connector and called the result the S-100 slot.
claims.quote_verbatim: That become the S100 industry slot because the connector used in the Altair had 100 pins on it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: 555 Contest, Computer Museum, Octopart - The Green Pen Hornswoggle

claims.claim_text: Designing a product around an off-the-shelf enclosure can mean cutting the specification to fit the case, for example dropping from four front-panel connectors to three rather than commissioning custom tooling.
claims.quote_verbatim: But I can't have, you know, four connectors on the front instead of three. Okay. Well, I'll change my project spec to three to make it fit.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: At gigabit signalling rates the cable and connector become more critical than they are at USB 2.0 speeds; a kink in the cable raises the bit error rate enough to drop the link entirely.
claims.quote_verbatim: once you get up to those sort of gigabit speeds, the, the, the cables are crucial. The connectors are crucial, even more so than USB 2.0.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Some HDMI cable assemblies are rated for as few as 20 mating cycles, a figure far below what a user would assume from experience with consumer charging cables.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've heard about HDMI cables before that had like 20, 20 insertions before they, they die. So that they're only rated at 20 plugging and unplugging.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A low-cycle connector can be destroyed within ten to twenty insertions if it is mated at the wrong angle or with the wrong amount of force, so the rated cycle count assumes correct insertion technique.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can kill them within, yeah, 10, 20 insertions if you got the wrong angle or something like that. The wrong amount of force at the wrong angle on the connector.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Connectors are sold in different grades of gold plating, with contact coatings specified in thicknesses such as 5, 10 and 20 microns; thicker plating buys mating-cycle life at higher unit cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can buy different grades of gold coating. You know, 5 microns, 10 microns, 20 microns thick.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGAs, Robots & Thermocouples - Wampum's Wavering Worth

claims.claim_text: Connector unit prices track the gold price directly, because the plating on the contacts is a real material cost; a rise in bullion prices moves a one-dollar part to roughly a dollar twenty.
claims.quote_verbatim: we were going to save you this for a buck, but gold's so expensive, it's a buck 20 now
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGAs, Robots & Thermocouples - Wampum's Wavering Worth

claims.claim_text: Image search is a practical way to find a connector whose name is unknown: type the closest description, such as the interface family, and scroll the results visually.
claims.quote_verbatim: The best way to do it still is Google image search, in my opinion. Type in what you think you need. I need an RJ45, and then just start scrolling.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Arduino, IndiGoGo and Hack-a-Day - Doodad Dealer Dancing

claims.claim_text: Molex, among the largest connector manufacturers in the world, was bought by the Koch business interests, consolidating a major share of the interconnect supply base under a new owner.
claims.quote_verbatim: Are buying Molex. Molex. Yeah. The huge connector company. Like the world's. Probably the world's biggest.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Agilent's New Name, Molex's New Owner and PCB artwork - Nonsensical Naming Neolatry

claims.claim_text: The commodity end of the connector market is heavily contested, with very large numbers of Shenzhen manufacturers building the same low-end part and each aiming to work its way up into higher-margin niches.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's 100,000 companies in Shenzhen, China right now making this exact same connector, and all of them dream to make the next level of connector, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Agilent's New Name, Molex's New Owner and PCB artwork - Nonsensical Naming Neolatry

claims.claim_text: Connector cost frequently dominates silicon cost on a board: a 16-channel data acquisition chip can cost around three dollars while a bulky plastic connector on the same design costs seven.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can buy a chip that does 16 channels of 80D measurement for like three bucks and I have to pay $7 for a big bulky plastic connector.
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: A modular product depends on the quality of its connection points for reliability, and even where there is no discrete connector the mating contact surfaces still require deliberate mechanical design.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you want to design and reliability into that, you need good connection points at least. Even if it's not a physical connector.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: Panel and board cutouts around connectors are routinely adjusted by fractions of a millimetre after first production, for example enlarging a hole by 0.2 mm where there is insufficient margin and a mounted part wobbles.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'd like that hole 0.2 millimeters bigger, because maybe there's not enough margin in the connector, and that switch wobbles just a little bit.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: A second-source connector is never an exact duplicate of the original, so it must be fully re-characterised; purpose-built automated insertion jigs mate the part a thousand times at varying angles to measure gold wear and expected life.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had to fully re-characterize and re-test those connectors. And they were different. You know, we designed automated insertion testing jigs. So, it would make these connectors a thousand times at different angles.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Connectors are harder to second-source than passives because compatibility is physical rather than electrical: a resistor can be moved from 0603 to 0805 with little consequence, while a connector change propagates into the mating part and the harness.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a physical compatibility thing. So, yeah, that's why it's a big deal with connectors. But, hey, you know, you can easily change, you know, your resistor from an 0603 to an 0805
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Once a local shop has been paid to tool a connector, it becomes the sole source and can raise prices, because re-tooling elsewhere means paying for tooling a second time and repeating the qualification work.
claims.quote_verbatim: And then they get to charge a healthy premium over what you were paying. Because they're it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Experienced engineers commonly recognise a connector on sight while being unable to recall its name, which makes visual catalogues and image-based searching more useful than text search for interconnect parts.
claims.quote_verbatim: I know a connector, but I won't know the name for it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Nadya Peek - Gallant Gcode Gerontology

claims.claim_text: A development board can be built with no connectors at all, with programming and sensor access carried over Bluetooth Low Energy so the module is entirely wireless and cannot be plugged into anything.
claims.quote_verbatim: really the most unique part of it is that it has no connectors. So there's no way – you actually can't plug it in. It's entirely wireless. So you can actually program it over BLE.
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Connectors qualified for military and emergency-services equipment can cost hundreds of dollars each, with prices around $900 per connector reported for such programmes.
claims.quote_verbatim: a sales guy telling me about a connector that costs $900 at an old place I used to work. We used to work on military and like firefighter electronics
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Space Bound, Again - Xtreme Xtraplanetary Xenonosocomiophobia

claims.claim_text: Unit prices of around $2,000 per connector occur on specialised products, driven by low production volumes together with the testing and certification burden rather than by material content.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've worked on products where they, where the, where there's $2,000 a connector. Right. And I mean, like, I get it, I get low volumes, I get like, you know, testing and certification and everything else like that.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Space Bound, Again - Xtreme Xtraplanetary Xenonosocomiophobia

claims.claim_text: A hundred watts cannot be pushed through a handful of thin twisted pairs in a small connector shell, so the power budget of a compact interface is set by contact and conductor cross-section rather than by protocol.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're not going to get a hundred watts through 10 twisted pairs, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Compare and Contrast Tech Entitlement - Worldly Working Wonks

claims.claim_text: High-power delivery over a small connector is achieved by raising the voltage rather than the current, because contact and conductor resistance make the equivalent power impossible to pass at five volts.
claims.quote_verbatim: They couldn't do this at five volts. You wouldn't physically be able to get the current through the connector. Right, right. Just because of resistance.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Compare and Contrast Tech Entitlement - Worldly Working Wonks

claims.claim_text: Five amps through a connector of small consumer size sits at the edge of what the contact geometry can support, leaving little margin for contact resistance growth.
claims.quote_verbatim: five amps is pushing it in a connector of this size, right? That's really pushing the boundaries
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Compare and Contrast Tech Entitlement - Worldly Working Wonks

claims.claim_text: A connector rated for 10,000 mating cycles is not necessarily rated to carry its full current after those cycles, because plating wear raises contact resistance as the gold rubs away.
claims.quote_verbatim: apparently this thing's rated for 10,000 cycles, so they claim. But I would love to see it still transfer five amps after 10,000 cycles.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Compare and Contrast Tech Entitlement - Worldly Working Wonks

claims.claim_text: The availability of cheap ready-made cable assemblies is itself a reason to specify a particular connector; five-centimetre jumper leads sold five to a pack for under a dollar remove all in-house harness work.
claims.quote_verbatim: A five-pack of five-centimeter cables for 95 cents.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Building a product around an off-the-shelf single-board computer transfers cost into the interconnect: extra circuitry has to be plugged in through additional connectors, producing an awkward stacked form factor that is hard to mount.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to piss away your extra money on all the connectors and everything to plug all your boards into it. And you end up with some convoluted weird-ass form factor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Keeping a mental library of connectors encountered in teardowns and catalogues pays off later, since knowing that a suitable part exists avoids designing a custom connector or settling for a worse solution.
claims.quote_verbatim: Connectors in particular, yeah, I'm always coming across weird connector requirements. So just knowing in the back of my mind, yes, something does exist that I've definitely seen it. I don't have to make a custom connector.
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Searching for an unfamiliar connector works best by assembling enough descriptive attributes — orientation, pitch, and mounting style, such as a right-angle two-millimetre-pitch edge connector — and running them through an image search.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you can figure at least something that's like, you know, right-angled, two-millimeter pitch edge connect, or, you know, if you can get enough words to describe it and just go through Google Image Search, you can quite quickly find something
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: A useful search strategy for interconnect parts is to find any vendor making something similar, learn the family term they use for it, such as mezzanine connector, and then search on that term to reach the correct product category.
claims.quote_verbatim: Sometimes it's even just finding a vendor being like, they might do something. Or finding something similar. Find out what they call it and then doing a search on that term.
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: On a small daisy-chained modular board the connectors, rather than the firmware, can be the hardest design problem, because the interconnect must not dominate the board outline.
claims.quote_verbatim: the hardest thing we've had to consider were the, were the connectors though
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

claims.claim_text: Fitting seven four-position connectors onto a 30 by 60 millimetre board while carrying close to one amp per link constrains the choice to parts compatible with 26 AWG wire, since the chain must power a servo at its far end.
claims.quote_verbatim: we want to be able to handle close to an amp if we can, you know, so we're trying to use 26 gauge wire
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

claims.claim_text: Feeding a board at 24 volts and stepping down to 5 volts with an on-board buck converter keeps the current through the input connector low enough that the housing does not melt.
claims.quote_verbatim: I found a 24 volt power supply and then I have an onboard buck that'll take that down to five volt and then that way the connector doesn't melt on me.
claims.speaker: Jason Cerundolo

claims.claim_text: Connectors used for permanent internal wiring are often rated for only ten to thirty mating cycles, which is acceptable while two devices are hardwired but not once the user is given a removable cable.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had just sort of hardwired them and connected them internally with a connector that's good for, say, 10 or 30 cycles
claims.speaker: Jason Cerundolo

claims.claim_text: Delivering 350 kilowatts to a single vehicle at 800 volts and 450 amps requires a purpose-designed connector, because at those currents every micro-ohm of contact resistance turns into significant dissipation.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's doing it at 800 volts, 450 amps.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Debug connector pin count sets how much visibility is available: a 20-pin header exposes full trace information, while a five-pin JTAG or two-to-three-pin SWD footprint still yields useful but reduced access.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you had a 20 pin connector, it would be really nice. You'd get all this information. But even with a five pin JTAG style connector or even a two or three pin SWD style, you still get some of this.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Double-row pin headers are generally at least five millimetres wide while single-row equivalents can be found under two and a half millimetres, which constrains board edge space on small modules.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just can't figure out why all of the double row headers are at least five millimeters wide, whereas we can find the single row headers smaller than two and a half millimeters wide.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: Dual-row plastic header bodies frequently measure wider than the manufacturer's published dimension, so mechanical clearances around them should be checked against physical samples rather than the datasheet alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: all the dual row plastic ones are, they're wider than they say in the spec
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: A custom connector justifies building a dedicated insertion rig that mates the part automatically, since real-world reliability depends on repeated insertions rather than on a single bench trial.
claims.quote_verbatim: Especially with custom connectors. You design a custom connector. You want to design a rig that just inserts this thing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A modular architecture always requires many connectors, and high-density parts such as an 80-pin Hirose board-to-board series push the unit cost of a modular system well above an equivalent monolithic board.
claims.quote_verbatim: the thing is modular always needs lots of connectors, right? Yeah. And I was using Hirose, like 80 pin.
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The Molex Micro-Fit is a 3 mm pitch two-by-two power connector that latches and is keyed so that it cannot be mated the wrong way round, which is why it is chosen where board space is tight and reverse mating would be destructive.
claims.quote_verbatim: the only socket that would fit in that space was a Molex micro fit, which is a three millimeter pitch, two by two plug in. So you plug it in, it clicks down and the connector is keyed. So you can't plug it in the wrong way around.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Substituting a third-party housing for the genuine part can defeat keying: copies with slightly undersized keys allowed a two-by-two power connector to be forced in reversed, which was not possible with the original.
claims.quote_verbatim: the connector housings they used, which weren't Molex, were much easier to plug into the connector the wrong way around. Because the keying was just a little bit smaller.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Effective keying works partly through tactile feedback: on a correctly toleranced housing an attempted reverse insertion feels obviously wrong, and the latch also sits in the wrong place, which stops an assembler before damage occurs.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you tried to plug it in the wrong way around, the keying meant you, you know, it felt wrong.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Where a keyed connector can physically be mated reversed, one orientation may apply supply directly to a data input and destroy the first device in a chain; a series protection resistor on that input is a cheap defence.
claims.quote_verbatim: if we'd have seen that you could actually insert this connector the wrong way, I could have easily just put a protection resistor on that strip.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Field failures traced back to connectors are often multi-factor: subcontracted cable assembly, a slightly different production housing, remote installation and untrained assemblers each looked harmless alone but combined to produce a repeatable dead-input failure.
claims.quote_verbatim: Any one thing of those, you know, it had to be the combination of all those factors.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Obsolescence is among the largest long-term risks a connector introduces into a design, since the mating part and harness are locked to it and no electrical substitute exists.
claims.quote_verbatim: the biggest risk is actually, uh, the connector going obsolete

claims.claim_text: A low-cost equivalent of a spring-pin programming connector can be made by soldering pogo pins to a connector body and moulding hot glue around the joint to form a handle.
claims.quote_verbatim: with taking a connector, soldering the pogo pin to the connector and then molding over with the hot glue around to have a handle

claims.claim_text: Making a breakout board for every component used, fanning out to 2.5 mm pin headers, allows fine-pitch parts such as sub-millimetre BGAs to be exercised on a breadboard before committing to a layout.
claims.quote_verbatim: It breaks out to 2.5 millimeter pins, right?

claims.claim_text: Calibrating a test fixture models the leakage, attenuation and phase shift of its wiring and connectors up to the measurement plane, so the fixture's contribution can be backed out and only the device response remains.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can take what you actually measured and back out that all of the stuff that's just done to the test harness, you know, the wiring and the, and the connectors and all that stuff and understand exactly what the response of just your component is
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: Cheap online-sourced RF cables vary enough in quality to corrupt measurements, so a common bench practice is to physically segregate characterised good cables from unverified ones.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have a large bin right now of crappy cables and a very small bin of good cables and I keep them separate
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: In some industries a connector price of around $200 per unit is routine, so interconnect can be a first-order line item in the bill of materials rather than a rounding error.
claims.quote_verbatim: I come from an industry where, you know, $200 us connectors are the norm.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Navy-specified connectors are typically sole-source, all-metal parts made by a single approved manufacturer, which is a large part of why their unit price reaches hundreds of dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: It was like a specced by the Navy, you know, like, you know, the only one company made them. It was like all metal and like had like pins and ridiculousness.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A very expensive military connector is not automatically the highest-quality part available; its price often reflects a long custom specification document written for one application rather than superior contact design.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was just really custom for what they wanted, you know? And it had a spec doc as long as your, long as your leg

claims.claim_text: Letting purchasing chase a tenfold price reduction on a connector is a route to grey-market or counterfeit parts, with the consequences surfacing only after the units are built.
claims.quote_verbatim: you left it up to your purchasing department and they ordered these gray market parts, which are either fake or whatever
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: To remove a through-hole connector without damaging the board, break away the plastic housing first and then desolder the individual pins one at a time, which leaves the pads reusable.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's better just to, you know, knock, knock the plastic part off, go and then, you know, solder, desolder all the pins
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Military and aerospace equipment consolidates many links into one multi-way circular connector specifically so that a technician reconnecting a system after maintenance cannot plug the wrong cable into the wrong place.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want to have any, run any risk of plugging the wrong thing in to the wrong place when you reconnect it back in

claims.claim_text: Multi-way military connectors carrying hundreds of individual pins require a wiring drawing that documents every pin, since unlike a structured interface such as Ethernet there is no implicit pairing to fall back on.
claims.quote_verbatim: at least some of these things have hundreds of pins attached to them. And it's like, yeah, you gotta, you gotta have a drawing for each and every pin

claims.claim_text: Hand-terminating a large multi-pin circular connector takes on the order of one to two hours per connector, a labour cost that dominates the harness build.
claims.quote_verbatim: it'd take you an hour or two hours to terminate one of these connectors

claims.claim_text: Splitting one large board into smaller boards joined by high-density board-to-board connectors can be cheaper overall than a single oversized bare PCB, even at a couple of dollars per connector against a hundred-dollar panel.
claims.quote_verbatim: even if you pay a couple of bucks per connector, it's still cheaper than paying for that one giant $100 bare PCB
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Mixed imperial and metric dimensioning causes mechanical stack-up errors: enclosures built to 19-inch rack standards force fractional-inch standoff heights that do not line up with metric connector stack heights.
claims.quote_verbatim: But then the connectors that stacked up to the same height as the standoffs, it just, it didn't line up.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: Connector manufacturers build many of their parts to order from large permutation spaces of pin counts, orientations and platings, which is why their catalogues contain vastly more part numbers than are ever stocked.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of these, uh, connector companies, especially they build so many of their components on the fly, right. They're all made to order and there's so many different permutations
claims.episode_title: Footprints and Symbols with Natasha Baker

claims.claim_text: The recommended sequence for a network measurement is to connect and measure first with no calibration, sanity-check the result, then adjust cables, connectors and adapters and wiggle the part to confirm stability, and only then calibrate.
claims.quote_verbatim: the first thing you do is you make all your measurements that you want to make without doing any calibration. Then you adjust your cables, your connectors, your adapters. Wiggle your part to make sure it's stable.
claims.speaker: Joel Dunsmore

claims.claim_text: An amplifier connected backwards shows up immediately as gain and isolation swapping sign, for example minus 30 dB of gain with plus 30 dB of isolation, which is why an uncalibrated sanity measurement is worth taking first.
claims.quote_verbatim: No, my gain's minus 30 dB on my amplifier. My isolation's plus 30. I hooked it up backwards.
claims.speaker: Joel Dunsmore

claims.claim_text: Whether to use connectors throughout or hardwire cables is a long-standing product-design decision; hardwiring saves unit cost but soldered-in cables must be desoldered before boards can be separated for service or analysis.
claims.quote_verbatim: They've like hardwired in these cables, right? They're soldering them in. And how do I get these boards apart?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: For test fixtures where peripherals are connected and disconnected repeatedly, a pluggable connector gives a more reliable joint than a ribbon cable that has been hand-soldered and desoldered several times.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've de-soldered that ribbon cable a couple of times and you know, my soldering is just, it's ugly.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Connector housings can be melted by an over-hot reflow or rework profile, so the temperature rating of the plastic body is a limit on the process window as much as the solder alloy is.
claims.quote_verbatim: It was a little too hot. I kind of melted some of my connectors.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: High-density board-to-board interconnect at the fine end uses parts such as a 100-position Hirose series at 0.4 mm pitch, arranged as 50 contacts per side and requiring a mating pair on each board.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's a Hirose, a high-density Hirose, 100 position.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: ESD protection belongs physically close to the connector it defends and must be rated for the working voltages of that interface.
claims.quote_verbatim: ESD protection should be placed, for example, close to a connector. It should be rated appropriate to what voltages you'll be working with.
claims.speaker: Philip Salmony
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Choosing an ESD protection device depends on the bus or signal speed, the frequencies of interest and the operating voltages, so a part suitable for one connector interface may load or distort another.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's actually quite a lot of detail to choosing the right ESD protection, you know, depending on what bus speeds or signal speeds you're using, uh, what frequencies you're interested in or what voltages you're running at.
claims.speaker: Philip Salmony
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Handling physical connector samples conveys scale, latch feel and mating action in a way distributor listings cannot, which is why sample cases carried by manufacturers' representatives remain a useful selection aid.
claims.quote_verbatim: there is nothing like my favorite thing in the world, which I still miss is when people would roll in the suitcase full of connectors and you just palm through it
claims.episode_title: Return of the Trade Show Jedi

claims.claim_text: Keeping pin headers, both straight and right-angle, in dedicated standing lab drawers rather than in per-project bags keeps interconnect stock available across projects instead of being consumed by one build.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got pin headers, right. I've got, you know, right angle pin headers, straight pin headers, right. They're in dedicated drawers. They're not in my project bags.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Fitting a mating two-pin pluggable pair to battery and switch leads, rather than soldering them directly, keeps the joint serviceable; pre-crimped wires inserted into two-pin housings are the stock item that makes this practical.
claims.quote_verbatim: I want to have a mating two pin pluggable pair there, right? So like batteries or a switch or something like that.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Connector manufacturer drawings are rarely dimensioned from the part centre, which makes placing the footprint origin awkward and forces the designer to derive pin positions from edge dimensions.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's never like dimensioned off center. You know, like all I really want to know is like, where do I put zero, zero on my footprint
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Engineering Education with Dr Don Wilcher

claims.claim_text: An automotive wiring harness drawing documents the connectors and the diameter and length of each branch bundle rather than individual wires, with separate prints giving the pinouts of each connector.
claims.quote_verbatim: The drawing is going to basically consist of the connectors and it's going to show not the individual wires, but it's going to show the diameter of the bundle that branches off the main wire harness.
claims.speaker: Don Wilcher
claims.episode_title: Engineering Education with Dr Don Wilcher

claims.claim_text: Automotive harness contacts are retained by small barbs, so removing or replacing a pin requires the manufacturer's dedicated extraction tool rather than improvised pulling.
claims.quote_verbatim: They had special tools cause the pins had like little barbs on the actual pins.
claims.speaker: Don Wilcher
claims.episode_title: Engineering Education with Dr Don Wilcher

claims.claim_text: Large vehicle manufacturers historically sourced their harness connectors from a single key in-house supplier, which later branched out to serve other automotive makers and held all the connector prints and pinouts.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were the, the key supplier of, you know, all connectors and they start branching off to other automotive
claims.speaker: Don Wilcher
claims.episode_title: Engineering Education with Dr Don Wilcher

claims.claim_text: Fifty-mil-pitch 100-pin board-to-board connectors used for daughterboard modules are expensive and chronically hard to source, and a design needing a mating pair of them carries that supply risk twice over.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's a .05. There's a 50 mil pitch connector. And those are hard to get. Those are unobtainium still too.

claims.claim_text: Reusing a standard connector housing for a non-standard interface, such as an RJ45 that is not Ethernet, invites a user to plug in a genuine cable and creates a mis-mating hazard that no marking fully removes.
claims.quote_verbatim: You think that, oh, this is an RJ 45, right? It must be an ethernet and you plug it in. No, it's some custom bloody, you know, interface.

claims.claim_text: Instruments returned as faulty are sometimes found to have nothing more than an internal connector deliberately unplugged, which is why reseating internal connectors is a first step before deeper repair work.
claims.quote_verbatim: a connector had been pulled and it's not like it vibrated loose
claims.speaker: Ian Johnston

claims.claim_text: Even a first revision with no electrical mistakes usually needs a respin, because manufacturability and access in deployment reveal that some connectors should be placed differently once the design is viewed from the user's side.
claims.quote_verbatim: you would like to, you know, optimize, for example, some connectors should be placed differently, right? Because now you are, you started thinking from user point of view
claims.speaker: Pallav Aggarwal

claims.claim_text: A connector footprint can be placed with the component rotated exactly 180 degrees while still appearing perfectly aligned on the board, a layout error that no automated design check catches.
claims.quote_verbatim: turns out that I rotated the component, the connectors, despite them being perfectly lined up, they were rotated exactly 180 degrees
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: When an assembly house is out of stock of a connector, one workable response is to omit it from the assembly order and hand-solder the part later rather than delay the whole build.
claims.quote_verbatim: there was another connector that was on board that I was pretty sure they didn't have, but then this was right that they were out. So I just left off the board and I'm going to hand solder those later.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The existing connector literature is written by connector designers rather than connector users, leaving no single reference covering the full range of interconnect from the specifying engineer's point of view.
claims.quote_verbatim: there are books about connectors, but they're from the point of view of people who design the connectors, not from the people who use the connectors
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: Contact corrosion is a common way connector knowledge is learned the hard way: submerging a cable assembly or leaving it exposed in a high-humidity environment degrades the contact interface.
claims.quote_verbatim: You learn about like corrosion on contacts and things like it by like being like, oh, yeah, no, maybe I shouldn't submerge that cable or have it exposed in a high humidity environment.
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: Insulation-displacement ribbon-cable termination depends on a proprietary hand tool costing around $150, of which a workshop typically owns exactly one, making the tool a bottleneck for harness work.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's always that $150 hand tool that they want to sell you, and that you have one of
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: The insulation-displacement connector crimped onto the end of a ribbon cable has no accepted generic name, which is one reason interconnect parts are hard to search for by description.
claims.quote_verbatim: The connector at the end of that ribbon cable does not have a name.
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: When the mating part is already known, searching on the part's own name plus the word connector and reading a published schematic is faster than working down a connector classification tree.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you already know the part, I would say the best thing to do is to go and search for, like, I know it's CM4. I would go search for, like, CM4 connector and probably find a schematic.
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: Connector proliferation is a consequence of physics rather than poor standardisation: no single connector can both carry vehicle-charging currents and present the constant impedance and high-frequency response an antenna feed requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: if we only had one connector, we couldn't charge our car with a USB connector because it doesn't carry enough current. We couldn't connect the antenna to your TV with a USB because it doesn't have the high frequency response and constant impedance.
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea
